The most famous telescope in the world is falling out of the sky. And NASA is asking for help.
Hubble has been circling Earth since 1990. It's about the size of a school bus.
It showed us galaxies so far away, their light left before Earth even existed.
But even up there, there's a tiny bit of air. And every day, it drags Hubble a little lower.
Hubble has no engine. Space shuttle astronauts used to visit, fix it, and push it back up.
But the last visit was in 2009. Since then, nobody can reach it.
NASA estimates Hubble could fall back into the atmosphere around 2033.
So on October twenty ninth, NASA asked companies for ideas.
Grab it and push it higher. Repair and upgrade it. Or steer it safely into a remote ocean.
Companies have until November thirtieth to answer.
NASA has said no to a rescue before. It's expensive, and a bad docking could break the telescope.
Any mission would need to fly by 2032.
So the next few years decide whether Hubble gets a second life, or a final splash.
